narrative_purpose: Teaches the two architectures of the root-fungus handshake side by side: the arbuscular type, where the fungus pushes inside the root cells and branches into tree-shaped arbuscules, versus the ectomycorrhizal type, where the fungus sheathes the root tip and threads between the cells without entering them — the real trading desks where carbon and phosphorus change hands.
subject: A clean two-panel cutaway. Left panel: a root cross-section with fungal threads penetrating individual root cells and ballooning inside them into finely branched, tree-shaped arbuscules. Right panel: a root tip wrapped in a dense fungal sheath or mantle, with a net of threads running between the outer cells but not piercing them. From both, fine hyphae radiate outward into the surrounding soil.
scene: A microscopic-anatomy view, the two root sections floating on a dark page with soil texture suggested faintly behind.
camera: A close, clean scientific-illustration view of two root cross-sections at matched scale.
light: Even diagrammatic light on the root structures; the fungal arbuscules and mantle picked out in a soft cyan-teal glow to read as the living interface.
palette: Muted root tones in dim teal-grey, the fungal structures in luminous Pandora cyan and living teal against void-indigo.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate with strong diagrammatic clarity, hand-painted texture.
detail_level: Crisp and detailed on both root cross-sections and the fungal structures inside/around them; soft elsewhere.
composition: Two balanced panels left and right at matched scale, clear separation between them, dark margins for callout labels.
consistency_notes: Pure Earth-science figure rendered in the book's cool palette and from-within glow so it sits beside the Pandoran plates; the arbuscule-inside-cell vs mantle-around-cell contrast must read clearly; leave open dark space beside each panel for labels.
